title: Word RAM acceptance implies nondeterministic space membership
statement: Let $P$ be an extended Word RAM program, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $W,T_W,S_W,F:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose a finite Turing machine computes the word width $W(n)$ in at most $T_W(n)$ steps and space $S_W(n)$. Suppose that for every input $x$ there is a time bound $t$ such that, for every coin string, $P$ halts within $t$ steps using words of width $W(|x|)$ and at most $F(|x|)$ touched addresses, and $x\in L$ exactly when some coin string and output yield acceptance within those bounds. If, for every $n$, $S_W(n)+F(n)(W(n)+1)+W(n)+(\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1)+1\le a s(n)$ for natural numbers $a$ and every $n$, then $L$ belongs to nondeterministic space $\mathrm{NSPACE}(s)$.
hypotheses_covered: An extended Word RAM program $P$ and Boolean language $L$
Functions $W,T_W,S_W,F$ from natural numbers to natural numbers
A Turing machine computes $W(n)$ within time $T_W(n)$ and space $S_W(n)$
For every input, a time bound $t$ works for all coin strings
Halting within $t$ steps at width $W(|x|)$ and with at most $F(|x|)$ touched addresses
Membership in $L$ is equivalent to existence of an accepting coin-string run within those bounds
